title: Payment API elevated 503 errors after v2.8.1
summary: payment-api returned HTTP 503 for 38% of authorisation requests six minutes after a routine deploy. Redis connection waits timed out because the client pool saturated.
root_cause: payment-api v2.8.1 added an idempotency lookup that issued two extra Redis calls per request without raising the client pool. The 50-connection pool saturated, requests blocked on connection checkout, and the service shed them as 503.
resolution: Rolled back to v2.8.0 to stop the bleeding, then re-released v2.8.2 with the Redis client pool raised from 50 to 100 connections per replica.
symptoms: redis client 'timeout waiting for connection from pool' errors
Redis server CPU and memory flat

events.description: Deployed payment-api v2.8.1 to production (8 replicas, rolling).
HTTP 503 rate crossed 5% and continued climbing to 38%.
Client-side pool checkout timeouts; pool reported 50/50 in use on every replica.
Alert PAY-5XX fired to the payments on-call.
Error rate returned to baseline as rollback completed.

actions.note: Immediate mitigation.
Sized for the extra calls per request. Replica count was not considered.

title: Redis cluster refused connections after payment-api pool increase
summary: redis-cache reached maxclients and rejected new connections across several services. The 100-connection pool from INC-1042 was multiplied by 14 payment-api replicas.
root_cause: The larger client pool from INC-1042 was correct per replica but not in aggregate. After autoscaling to 14 replicas, payment-api alone held 1,400 of the 1,500 configured Redis maxclients, so redis-cache refused connections to payment-api, checkout-api, and notification-worker.
resolution: Reduced the payment-api Redis client pool from 100 to 30 connections per replica and left maxclients unchanged. Aggregate pool sizing was added to the deploy checklist.
symptoms: redis-cache 'ERR max number of clients reached'
connection errors on checkout-api and notification-worker as well

events.description: p99 latency doubled without any deploy in the preceding four hours.
Redis returned 'max number of clients reached' to new connections.
503 rate reached 12%; checkout-api began failing as well.
Alert REDIS-MAXCLIENTS fired to the platform on-call.
Rolled the Redis client pool down to 30 per replica.

actions.note: Dependency-side saturation, not app-side exhaustion. Directly reverses INC-1042.

title: Payment API 503 errors and Redis timeouts after v1.4.2
summary: payment-api returned 503 and logged Redis timeouts minutes after a deploy. Redis was refusing connections at its configured maxclients ceiling.
root_cause: payment-api v1.4.2 opened a Redis connection per worker thread instead of sharing a pool. The single Redis node hit its maxclients ceiling of 4000 and refused further connections.
resolution: Raised maxclients in redis.conf from 4000 to 10000 and restarted the Redis node during a maintenance window. The per-thread connection behaviour was fixed in a later release.
tech_context: single Redis node, no cluster mode

events.description: Redis refused new connections at maxclients.

actions.note: Single-node Redis 5 configuration; the cluster no longer runs this way.
Required a maintenance window on the single node.

title: Staging payment-api 503 errors after v2.9.0-rc1
summary: Release candidate in staging produced 503 errors and Redis pool timeouts. Contained to staging; no customer impact.
root_cause: v2.9.0-rc1 shipped with the Redis pool size left at the staging default of 10, which is too small for the load-test profile.
resolution: Set the staging Redis pool to match the production value and re-ran the load test.

events.description: Pool checkout timeouts against the staging Redis instance.
Staging alert routed to the release channel, not to on-call.

actions.note: Staging-only configuration drift.

title: Ledger service exhausted Postgres connections during settlement
summary: ledger-service settlement batch opened more connections than pgbouncer allowed, stalling ledger writes and slowing payment-api captures.
root_cause: The nightly settlement batch runs one connection per shard. A shard split raised the shard count from 32 to 64 while the pgbouncer pool stayed at 40, so half the workers blocked waiting for a server connection.
resolution: Raised the pgbouncer pool from 40 to 80 and capped batch concurrency at the pool size.

events.description: Settlement batch step latency rose sharply.

actions.note: Batch concurrency capped at the same number.

title: Checkout latency from Redis key eviction
summary: checkout-api latency tripled because redis-cache was evicting live cart sessions under memory pressure.
root_cause: redis-cache reached its 4GB maxmemory limit. With allkeys-lru, Redis evicted active cart sessions alongside cache entries, so checkout-api rebuilt carts from Postgres on most requests.
resolution: Raised maxmemory from 4GB to 8GB and moved cart sessions to a logical database with volatile-lru so only keys with a TTL can be evicted.
symptoms: cart cache hit rate fell from 94% to 38%

events.description: Cache misses and slow GETs as evictions accelerated.

actions.note: Applied to the session database only.

title: Notification queue backlog during campaign send
summary: notification-worker fell behind the Redis queue during a marketing campaign; delivery lag reached 40 minutes.
root_cause: Four worker replicas could not drain a campaign enqueueing 9,000 messages per minute. Queue depth grew monotonically and the workers began timing out on Redis blocking pops.
resolution: Scaled notification-worker from 4 to 10 replicas and added a queue-depth based autoscaler.

events.description: Worker BRPOP calls timed out under queue pressure.

actions.note: Sized for the campaign send rate.

title: Notification workers saturated Postgres after scale-out
summary: The ten notification-worker replicas from INC-1120 exhausted Postgres connections during a nightly batch, blocking ledger writes.
root_cause: Ten replicas each hold a 20-connection Postgres pool. Overlapping with the settlement batch, that left no headroom in pgbouncer and ledger-service writes blocked. The scale-out from INC-1120 was sized for Redis throughput, not for Postgres connections.
resolution: Reduced notification-worker from 10 to 5 replicas and moved the campaign send outside the settlement window.

events.description: Worker job duration rose as connection checkout blocked.
pgbouncer had no free server connections.
Ledger write errors from connection timeouts.

actions.note: Dependency-side connection limit, not worker throughput. Reverses INC-1120.

title: Auth API total outage during Postgres failover
summary: Postgres primary failed and Patroni did not promote the replica, leaving auth-api unable to issue sessions for 26 minutes.
root_cause: The primary Postgres node lost its storage volume. Patroni held a stale leader lock because its TTL was longer than the detection window, so automatic promotion did not run and every login failed.
resolution: Promoted the replica manually, then lowered the Patroni leader TTL and loop interval so detection completes inside the alerting window.

events.description: Primary node stopped responding to health checks.
Alert AUTH-DOWN paged identity and database on-call.
Login success rate back to baseline.

actions.note: Manual promotion.
Detection window shortened.

title: Redis primary failover caused cross-service timeouts
summary: A redis-cache primary node failed over. Clients that cached the topology kept dialling the old node, so payment-api, checkout-api, and auth-api all saw dependency timeouts.
root_cause: The primary shard node was terminated by the cloud provider. Failover completed in 40 seconds, but client libraries with a 300-second topology refresh kept sending writes to the old address until they were restarted.
resolution: Failover completed automatically. Client topology refresh was lowered to 30 seconds and a second replica was added per shard.
symptoms: dependency timeouts on payment-api, checkout-api, and auth-api at the same minute
Redis MOVED and connection refused errors
no deploy in the preceding 12 hours

events.description: Primary shard node stopped accepting connections.
Clients restarted to pick up the new topology.

actions.note: Automatic.
Per shard.

title: Payment API 503 errors from expired upstream certificate
summary: payment-api returned 503 on captures because the ledger-service TLS certificate expired. No deploy was involved.
root_cause: The ledger-service internal TLS certificate expired at 02:12. Certificate rotation had been excluded from the automation when the service moved namespaces, so nothing renewed it.
resolution: Issued and deployed a new certificate, then re-registered the service with the rotation automation.
symptoms: no deploy in the preceding 30 hours

events.description: TLS handshake failures began at the exact certificate expiry minute.

title: Payment API 503s in eu-west-1 during a regional traffic shift
summary: payment-api in eu-west-1 returned 503 on authorisations after a planned traffic shift moved most European volume onto a region provisioned for a fraction of it. Redis client pools filled first.
root_cause: The traffic shift tripled request volume in eu-west-1 without scaling payment-api there. Per-replica Redis client pools exhausted under the extra load; Redis itself had headroom.
resolution: Shifted traffic weight back toward ap-south-1 and scheduled regional capacity before the next shift.
symptoms: redis client timeout waiting for connection from pool

events.description: eu-west-1 p99 latency rose as shifted traffic arrived.
Redis pool checkout timeouts in eu-west-1 pods.
Alert PAY-5XX-EU paged the payments on-call.

actions.note: Region capacity, not pool size, was the constraint.

title: Postgres primary disk pressure from WAL retention
summary: WAL files filled the primary data volume to 96%, putting the cluster minutes away from refusing writes.
root_cause: A stalled logical replication slot stopped WAL recycling. With wal_keep_size set generously, retained WAL grew until the volume was nearly full.
resolution: Dropped the abandoned replication slot, expanded the volume from 500GB to 1TB, and reduced wal_keep_size.
symptoms: inactive replication slot with growing lag

events.description: Write latency rose as the volume approached full.
Abandoned replication slot dropped; WAL began recycling.

title: Payment API slow queries after a dropped index
summary: A migration dropped an index still used by the authorisation lookup, so payment-api latency rose without any error rate change.
root_cause: Migration 2026_08_25_drop_unused_indexes removed idx_authorisations_merchant_created, which the authorisation history query still used. The planner fell back to a sequential scan over 40 million rows.
resolution: Recreated the index concurrently and added a planner check to the migration review.
symptoms: p99 latency 3.4x baseline with a flat error rate

actions.note: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY.

title: Ledger service thread pool exhaustion after v3.1.0
summary: ledger-service stopped accepting work after a deploy moved a blocking call onto the request thread pool.
root_cause: v3.1.0 made the settlement reconciliation call synchronously on the request thread pool. With 32 threads, a slow upstream response blocked every thread and the service queued requests until they timed out.
resolution: Rolled back to v3.0.7, then re-released with the call moved off the request pool and the pool raised from 32 to 64 threads.
symptoms: ledger-service request queue depth at limit
thread pool active count pinned at 32

events.description: Request latency rose sharply as the thread pool filled.

actions.note: Secondary to moving the blocking call off the pool.

title: Auth API rate limiter rejected valid traffic after v4.2.0
summary: A deploy shipped a per-tenant rate limit as a global limit, so auth-api returned 429 to most login attempts.
root_cause: v4.2.0 read the rate limit from a key that lost its per-tenant scope during a config refactor. The 100 requests per second limit applied to the whole service instead of to each tenant.
resolution: Rolled back to v4.1.6 and restored the per-tenant scope, with the effective limit raised to 1000 requests per second.
symptoms: rate limiter counter shared across tenants

actions.note: Per tenant, restoring the original scope.

title: Storefront 5xx from a CDN cache rule change
summary: A CDN rule change cached error responses, so frontend-web served stale 5xx pages after the origin had recovered.
root_cause: A cache rule added a TTL for 5xx responses. A brief origin blip was cached and then served to every visitor for the rest of the TTL.
resolution: Removed the 5xx caching rule and purged the CDN.
symptoms: frontend-web error pages while the origin was healthy

title: Staging checkout rollback drill
summary: Planned game-day exercise validating the checkout-api rollback runbook in staging.
root_cause: Deliberately introduced fault during a rollback drill. Not a real defect.
resolution: Followed RB-22 and rolled back within the target window. Two runbook steps were clarified afterwards.

actions.note: Exercise only.

title: Duplicate notifications from overlapping cron runs
summary: A long digest run overlapped the next scheduled run, so some recipients received the same digest twice.
root_cause: The digest cron had no concurrency guard. When a run exceeded its 15-minute interval, the next run started against the same unmarked rows.
resolution: Moved the schedule to hourly and added a Redis lock so only one run can be active.
symptoms: two overlapping worker runs in the logs

events.description: Duplicate send rate rose above zero.

actions.note: Plus a Redis lock.

title: Postgres autovacuum lag and table bloat
summary: Autovacuum fell behind on the authorisations table, so bloat grew and query plans drifted.
root_cause: Three autovacuum workers could not keep up with the write rate on the authorisations table after a traffic increase. Dead tuples accumulated and the planner's estimates degraded.
resolution: Raised autovacuum_max_workers from 3 to 6, lowered the scale factor on the hot table, and ran a manual vacuum.
symptoms: table size growing faster than row count

events.description: Alert PG-BLOAT fired on the authorisations table.
Autovacuum workers raised and manual vacuum started.
